name: Voicemail Replacement
h1: Replace Voicemail With an AI Agent That Takes Real Messages
metaDescription: Swap the beep for a conversation. A Calldesk agent asks follow-up questions, captures name, number and reason, and sends you a summary, not audio.
intro: Voicemail asks the caller to do the work: speak to a recording, remember to state a name and number, and explain the problem clearly with no one to ask what they mean. Many callers hang up at the beep, and those who stay often mumble a number or leave out what the call is about. For the owner, the box becomes a chore of replaying audio on a bad day to find who needs a callback first. A message-taking agent replaces the beep with a short conversation. It says it is an AI assistant, explains that nobody is available, and asks for the same few things every time: name, a number to reach them, what it is about, and how urgent. If the answer is thin it asks a follow-up question, and it repeats the callback number back so a wrong digit is caught while the caller is still there. What you receive is a written summary, the extracted fields and a transcript, instead of an audio file in a queue, and a call-completed webhook can push it to email or your helpdesk. The message-taking template covers the pattern, and it works alongside forwarding rules so that your phone sends unanswered calls to the agent.
steps: Create an agent from the message-taking template, which collects name, callback number and reason for the call, and edit the opening so it says nobody is available.
Add extraction fields for anything your team always has to chase, such as preferred time to call, account number or preferred contact method.
Write an urgency question with clear edge conditions, and decide which urgent callers should be transferred to a mobile number and which are logged for the next working day.
Keep the read-back of the callback number, so digits are confirmed while the caller is on the line.
Get a number for the agent, bring your own or add one from Calldesk, and set your phone system to forward unanswered calls to it instead of to the old voicemail box.
Register a call-completed webhook, in flat format if your tool prefers it, so each message lands in email, your CRM or your helpdesk with the summary attached.
Place test calls, including a caller who gives an unclear number, and refine the follow-up questions.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: You've reached Calloway Accounting. Nobody is available to take your call right now. I'm an AI assistant and I can take a message. May I have your name?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks, Greg. What's a good number for a call back?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Five five five, zero one eight eight.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Let me read that back: five five five, zero one eight eight. Is that right?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: And what is the call about?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: I got a letter from the tax office and I'm not sure what to do.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Understood. Is there a date on the letter that you need to respond by?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I've noted a tax office letter with a response date of the fifteenth. Someone will call you back. Goodbye, Greg.

featuresUsed.howItHelps: Name, callback number, reason and urgency are separate fields instead of a single audio file.
You read a short written message, with the transcript behind it, and no audio to replay.
A call-completed event can send each message to email, a helpdesk or a CRM as it arrives.
Urgent callers can be passed to a mobile number you choose, not just logged.

featuresUsed.feature: Bring your own number or carrier
featuresUsed.howItHelps: Unanswered calls are forwarded from your existing line to the agent without changing the number you publish.

featuresUsed.feature: Call testing and live call monitoring
featuresUsed.howItHelps: You can check how the agent handles vague answers before replacing your voicemail box.

considerations: Callers expect to leave a message, so state clearly that they are talking to an AI assistant and what will happen with their information.
Messages can contain private details. Decide who receives the summaries, how long you keep transcripts, and confirm any legal retention or consent requirements with counsel.
Forwarding to the agent changes where missed calls go. Keep your old voicemail as a fallback for the case in which the forwarding target is unreachable, if your carrier supports that.

faq.q: How is this different from visual voicemail?
faq.a: Visual voicemail still presents the caller's own recording. The agent asks questions, repeats the number back, and delivers a written summary plus fields, so there is nothing to transcribe.

faq.q: Can callers still leave a plain message?
faq.a: Yes. They answer the questions in their own words, and the transcript keeps everything they said.

faq.q: Do I get an alert when a message arrives?
faq.a: Use a call-completed webhook to send each summary to email or a chat tool. Calldesk also has an alerting section in the dashboard for call conditions.

faq.q: What if the caller hangs up midway?
faq.a: The call is still logged with whatever was captured and an outcome such as abandoned, so you can see partial messages.

faq.q: Is this the same as the after-hours page?
faq.a: They overlap. After-hours answering is about hours logic and emergencies at night. This page is about replacing the voicemail box itself, at any time nobody can pick up.
